interactions.summary: Participants read Dante's prophetic lines in English and Italian about humanity straying without a ruler and a future providential reversal that will set the fleet straight.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Participants reading Dante in English and Italian

interactions.summary: Jiang says astrology and astronomy matter because they encode cyclical cosmic movement, Aurelia hears circular vowels and seasonal return in the Italian, and Jiang says the language itself can generate subconscious images that connect the hearer to the divine.
The opening of Canto 28 is read in English and Italian, centering on a mirrored flame and truthful reflection.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Participants reading Dante in English and Italian

interactions.summary: Jiang stops the reading and asks the class to remember where the mirrored flame appeared before, stressing that it is important for the ending.

claims.claim: The quoted Dante passage says humanity strays because no king governs the earth, but a providential reversal will eventually straighten the fleet and bring true fruit after the flower.
Jiang says astrology and astronomy matter in the Divine Comedy because they register the cyclical movement of the universe.
Aurelia hears circularity in the vowels and a seasonal return in the verse, which supports Jiang's sense that the language itself can feel cyclical.
Jiang says that when one knows the Italian, meaning is captured in the language itself, so the sounds can generate subconscious images and excite a connection to the divine.
Jiang says the mirrored flame image is a major callback that Dante will use again at the very end as a metaphor for God.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang describes language as a divine image-engine: hear the right Italian and subconscious pictures bloom on their own.
signature_moments.source_phrase: images appear before you subconsciously and it excites your connection to the divine
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the packet's strongest articulation of sound becoming spiritual cognition.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang flags the mirrored flame as one of the ending's key metaphors for God and explicitly tells the class to carry it forward.
signature_moments.source_phrase: This is actually very important for the ending
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This preserves the packet's most important internal callback and future-facing interpretive anchor.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: A recurring Dante image Jiang identifies as a metaphor for God and a crucial callback near the poem's ending.

chronology_notes.note: Jiang explicitly frames the mirrored flame as a callback the class has already seen and as a symbol that will matter again at the end of the Divine Comedy.
